properties.decision:
RULED by Anthony 2026-09-06 ("go with your above recommendations for v0.50.0"), item 5 of the v0.50.0 plan: option (b) — the digest computed server-side, one call, deterministic, reply-cost bounded by the server — with option (a)'s skill reduced to a thin instruction leg that points at the tool and renders in the reader's domain; the not-found line mandatory; the reply budgeted like detect_gaps with `count` and `by_type` never trimmed. Option (c) (a topic argument on where-am-i) rejected as wrong-scoped; (d) is what he had. The tool takes the one naming convention (query, limit, budget_chars; nothing to name a node by). Shipped as cap:the-design-holds-about-one-subject-is-read-back-in-one-call.

WHAT WAS ON THE TABLE (recorded 2026-09-06 as brainstorming). Anthony, in his words: 'adding /topic or /topic-search skill — some times, I just want to see what's already within the reflow2 graph and it isn't a brainstorm or link-artifacts type effort — I just want to see something about a topic.' Distinct from dec:idea-should-the-open-list-be-rendered-in-the-owners-language-rather-than-the-graphs (qs): that renders the OPEN LIST in the owner's vocabulary; this renders the design's knowledge of ONE SUBJECT. Same family (a projection in the reader's words), different question.

WHAT EXISTED, and why it was not this: search_design returns ranked hits — ids and names, one dimension; get_node reads one node; where-am-i reads back the WHOLE design's state; relation_candidates and surprising_connections work outward from one node. None answered 'what do we know about X' as a digest: what is decided about it and why, what is still open, what has been measured, what realizes or checks it, and what is conspicuously absent.

OPTIONS AS RECORDED: (a) a served skill that runs search_design, groups by type, pulls each hit's neighbourhood and renders — cheapest to ship, 5-10 calls per topic, and two agents render one topic differently. (b) a tool `topic_report(query)` computed server-side — the SE doctrine on record (views are PURE PROJECTIONS of the graph and a renderer's fill-ins are defects) puts the projection in the server. (c) extend where-am-i with a topic argument. (d) nothing new.
properties.name: DECIDED — reflow2 serves the /topic view as a server-computed `topic_report(query)`: hits grouped by type, each with status, connections and the latest dated change or measurement, a MANDATORY not-found line, a bounded reply; a thin `topic` skill is its instruction leg
properties.rationale: COUNTER-ARGUMENTS beside each. (a) rests entirely on search quality, and search misses on the agent's phrasing were measured this week (dec:idea-search-expands-with-the-projects-own-domain-vocabulary): a topic digest built on a miss is a confident wrong answer about what the design holds, worse than a raw hit list, so the 'what was not found' line is load-bearing, not decoration. (a) also adds reply cost — fact:defect-the-reply-costs-more-than-the-answer is open — and a digest per topic that is not bounded becomes the verbose-reply problem in a new coat. (b) is the honest home by the projection doctrine and by cost (one call, server-bounded), but it is a new tool on a surface whose sibling-inconsistency is the largest open friction class — it must take the ONE naming convention Anthony just ruled (type optional, resolved from the id) from day one. (c) is free and wrong-scoped. (d) is what he has. A RANKING IS A FINDING, NOT A DECISION: (b) with a thin skill as its instruction leg, and the not-found line mandatory; (a) as the prototype that discovers what the digest should contain before the tool freezes it. Anthony rules — and nothing here is built until he does.
